definition: A measure of the hydroxide ion concentration of a solution: $\mathrm{pOH} = -\log_{10}[\ce{OH^-}]$, with $[\ce{OH^-}]$ in $\pu{mol dm-3}$; it has no units, and at 298 K $\mathrm{pH} + \mathrm{pOH} = 14.00$.

The equilibrium constant $K_\mathrm{a}$ for a weak acid ionizing in water, $K_\mathrm{a} = \frac{[\ce{H^+}][\ce{A^-}]}{[\ce{HA}]}$ (water left out); the larger it is, the stronger the acid, and it changes only with temperature.
The equilibrium constant $K_\mathrm{b}$ for a weak base taking a proton from water, $K_\mathrm{b} = \frac{[\ce{BH^+}][\ce{OH^-}]}{[\ce{B}]}$ (water left out); the larger it is, the stronger the base.
The negative logarithm to base 10 of the acid dissociation constant, $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = -\log_{10}K_\mathrm{a}$; a smaller pKa means a stronger acid.
